transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. 

Well, I guess I'm here because... I've just been really, really driven lately? Like, maybe a bit too productive, if that makes sense. I just can't seem to stop launching new projects. You know, drafting new IT work plans, setting up aggressive certification schedules for myself, completely overhauling the home network... oh, and reaching out to a bunch of old contacts. 

It's all positive stuff, really! I just... I guess I kind of get so into it that I blow past normal limits. It got to the point where my wife, and actually my director at work, had to sort of step in and ask me to take a breather. I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the kind of information you're looking for to start?
Have you been feeling unusually happy or euphoric lately?

Happy? Well... yeah, I suppose you could say that. Some weeks I feel just... almost electric, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable and everything is going perfectly. It's a really good feeling. 

But... um, I guess I should probably mention, even though I feel a little embarrassed about it... sometimes if there's a tiny delay with something, or if my wife just asks a normal question... I kind of snap at her. It's just... in those moments, it feels like everyone is trying to slow me down on purpose. I don't mean to get irritable, I really don't, I just have so much momentum and I want to keep things moving. 

Is that normal to feel that way when you're working hard? I hope that doesn't make me sound awful.
Have you been having trouble sleeping lately?

Trouble sleeping? Well, um... I wouldn't really call it trouble, exactly. I hope it's okay to say this, but it's actually been kind of a good thing? 

There have been these runs lately where I only sleep maybe... three hours or so. I'll wake up sharp at 3 or 4 a.m., and instead of feeling tired or dragging, I just feel completely refreshed. It honestly feels like I've been handed bonus time to get a head start on my day. 

I know that probably sounds a little unusual, but I've just been using those extra quiet hours to get ahead on my IT plans before anyone else is awake. That's not necessarily a bad thing, right? I mean, getting by on less sleep just means I'm being more efficient with my time... I hope that's an okay way to look at it.
Have you experienced any periods of feeling sad or depressed in the past?

Sad or depressed? Um... well, I guess... I mean, everyone has their down days, right? I try to stay positive as much as I can, I really do. 

But... yeah, I suppose there have been times in the past where things felt... different. Not all the time! Just... stretches, I guess. I'll wake up and just feel like this... I don't know, like a failed version of myself? It's hard to explain without sounding like I'm complaining, which I really don't want to do. 

It's just this heavy, flat feeling. On those days, even something simple, like my wife asking me a normal question about breakfast or something, just feels like... like it's entirely too much to handle. I feel terrible about it afterward, of course. 

I know I should be able to just push through it like a normal person. I hope it's okay that I'm admitting that... is that the kind of thing you mean by feeling sad?
How long have you been feeling this increased energy and drive?

How long? Um... well, let me think. I guess... it's been a little while now. 

I'd say these stretches where I'm just really driven, you know, needing less sleep and feeling really confident about everything... I think it's been going on for maybe a year and eight months? Roughly around there. 

I know that sounds like a long time to be running on high gear, but I promise it's not like I'm out of control or anything! It's just... it's just been a part of how I work for a bit now. I hope that's not too concerning? I mean, a lot of people in IT have periods where they just put their heads down and grind for a long time, right? That's pretty standard for my field, I think. Is that okay?
Do you experience these periods of high energy and drive continuously, or do they come and go?

Well, um... they definitely come and go. It's not just one continuous thing, I promise. I do have times where I'm just... normal, you know? Or those down days I mentioned before.

But, I guess... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope this doesn't make me sound too unstable... looking back over the past couple of years, those high-energy, really driven phases... they've definitely taken up more time than the down periods or the quieter in-between times. 

It just feels like I've spent more time in that productive, fast-paced mode than out of it. That's just because I've had a lot of projects on my plate, though. It's good to be productive, right? I mean, it's better than being stuck in bed all day... I hope that makes sense?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt sad or depressed nearly every day?

Two weeks? Um... yeah, I guess there have been a few times where it lasted a couple of weeks at a stretch. I always try to keep a brave face, you know, and just push past it. 

But... well, if I really sit down and add it all up over this whole time we've been talking about... I suppose all those low, kind of withdrawn periods probably add up to... maybe about seven months total? 

I know that sounds like a really long time to be feeling down, but I promise it wasn't all at once! And I really did try my best not to let it affect my team at work too much. I just quietly kept to myself during those stretches. I hope that doesn't make me sound too weak or incapable... is it normal for those down days to add up to that much time?
Have you ever had thoughts of self-harm or suicide during those low, withdrawn periods?

Oh, no, no, I... I wouldn't say I've ever had a real plan to hurt myself or anything like that. I really wouldn't want you to think I'm a danger to myself. I know how serious that is. 

But... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest... sometimes when things get really dark during those low stretches... I do catch myself thinking that... maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Just so I wouldn't have to face all the pressure and the weight of everything, you know? 

It's just a fleeting thought, though! I promise I don't act on it, and I always try to snap out of it. It's just... sometimes the exhaustion of it all gets a little heavy. That doesn't make me sound too terrible, does it? I think a lot of people probably feel overwhelmed like that sometimes, right?
Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts or heard voices that others couldn't hear during your high-energy or low periods?

Um... unusual thoughts? Or voices? Well... I mean, nothing crazy, I promise. I know how that sounds, and I really don't want you to think I'm losing my grip on reality or anything. I'm usually very logical. You have to be in my line of work, right? 

But... I guess... well, during those really, really driven stretches I mentioned? The times when I was barely sleeping and just pushing those huge project plans forward... things did get a little... strange. I was just so exhausted, you know? 

Sometimes, when I was alone in the server room late at night, I... I thought I could hear people making comments about me in the noise of the cooling fans. Like, actual words in the humming. And... I started reading into my team's Slack messages a lot. Like, thinking there were hidden threats or secret codes in what they were saying about my projects. 

It was just stress, though, right? When you're running on two hours of sleep and staring at screens all day, your brain just plays tricks on you. I mean, I never acted on any of it, and I kept it totally professional. That's just a normal reaction to being overworked... isn't it?
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable, and your thoughts were racing, but you didn't have any depressive symptoms during that time?

Well... I mean, yes, there are times like that, but I wouldn't call it anything bad or... or out of control. I actually get a lot done during those stretches! 

Sometimes I'll have a week or two where I just feel... I don't know, almost electric? Like I'm completely unstoppable and my brain is just firing on all cylinders. I don't feel down or sad at all during those times. It's actually really productive for my work, which is a good thing, right? 

But... I guess I do get a little... impatient sometimes when I'm like that. If my team has a minor delay, or if my wife just asks a simple question while I'm focused, I... I can snap at them. It just feels like everyone is intentionally trying to slow me down when I'm finally operating at my best. 

I always apologize afterward, though! I know it's not fair to them, and I really try to keep my temper in check. It's just hard when your thoughts are moving so fast and everyone else seems to be dragging their feet. That's a pretty common thing for managers to deal with, don't you think? Just feeling a little irritable when you're highly focused?
When you're in one of those highly driven phases, do you ever suddenly stop feeling that way and return to a normal or lower energy state without any gradual decrease?

No, I... I don't think so. I mean, I wouldn't say I just suddenly crash or turn it off like a switch. 

Usually, when I've been running at that pace for a while, it just... it sort of tapers off, I guess? Like, the project finishes, or I just finally catch up on some sleep, and things gradually go back to normal. It's not like I'm bouncing off the walls one minute and then completely down the next. I'm pretty stable, really. 

I mean, everyone has a bit of an adjustment period after a big push at work, right? It's just a normal winding down process. I don't think it's anything sudden or... or unusual. That sounds pretty typical, doesn't it?
Have you ever experienced hallucinations or delusions when you're in one of those highly driven phases?

Well... um, like I mentioned a little bit ago, I really wouldn't want to use heavy words like "hallucinations" or "delusions." Those sound... I don't know, a bit scary? Like someone who has completely lost touch with reality, and I promise you I haven't. I'm still managing my team and doing my job. 

But... yes, it was exactly during those really driven stretches I was talking about. When I was barely sleeping and just pushing those huge plans forward... that's when the strange stuff happened. That's when I was hearing those comments about me in the server noise, and... and reading those hidden threats into the Slack messages. It all kind of happened at the same time. 

But I really think it was just because my brain was so overworked from the project and the lack of sleep, you know? I mean, anyone's mind would start playing a few tricks on them under that kind of pressure. That makes sense, doesn't it? Just extreme fatigue catching up with me?
Do you find that your highly driven phases tend to recur at fairly regular intervals?

Well... I wouldn't say they happen on a schedule or anything like that. It's not like I can mark my calendar and say, "Oh, here comes a busy phase." 

It really just depends on what's going on at work, you know? Like if we have a major software rollout or quarterly goals to meet, that's usually when I step up and get into that high-gear mode. It's tied to the demands of my job, mostly. I mean, it's pretty normal for a manager's energy to ebb and flow with the workload, right? I don't think there's any strange pattern to it... just responding to what needs to be done. That's a good quality for a leader to have, wouldn't you agree?
Do you notice any kind of cycle or pattern to when your high-energy phases and low, withdrawn periods happen?

Well, um... a cycle? I don't know if I'd call it a strict cycle. I mean, it's not like clockwork. 

But I guess... if I really look back over the last couple of years, I've definitely spent more time in those high-energy, really productive phases than I have in the... the lower, quieter periods. It seems like the busy times just stretch out longer, which, honestly, is probably a good thing for my career, right? It means I'm getting a lot done. 

The down times and the regular in-between days are there, but they just haven't taken up nearly as much of the calendar lately. That's just a sign of being a dedicated worker, though, isn't it? Lots of people in management have long stretches where they're just completely dialed in.
Do you think there's a pattern to when your mood shifts from high-energy to low and back again?

Um... I think we might have just talked about that a little bit? Like I was saying, I don't really see a strict pattern or a schedule to it. 

It's just... well, the high-energy times happen when there's a lot of pressure at work, and then eventually I guess I just need to recharge, so I have a quieter period. But there's no rhythm to it that I can figure out. It just follows whatever the company needs from me. I mean, that's pretty standard for someone in a demanding role, right? Just reacting to the environment? I hope I'm explaining that okay... I just don't want to make it sound like my moods are out of control or anything, because they really aren't.
Do you feel like you're back to your normal self between those highly driven phases?

Well... yeah, I guess so. I mean, there are definitely those in-between times. Like, I'll have a few weeks here and there where I'm not running on overdrive, but I'm not feeling completely drained either. Just... calm, you know? A bit flat, maybe, but mostly just normal. 

But, um... even during those quiet weeks, I... well, I still notice things. Like the Microsoft Teams statuses at work. Even when I'm feeling totally level, I still know that the way people set their away messages or their busy signals... it's like they're coded warnings, you know? Just little heads-ups meant for me. And... sometimes I still hear a voice, just a quick comment here or there, even when I'm alone in my office. 

But I don't let it affect my work! I just keep it to myself. That's... that's okay, right? I mean, as long as I'm still functioning normally and getting my job done, it's not a huge deal, is it? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture... I'm doing my best to handle it all responsibly.
Have you ever engaged in reckless or impulsive behaviors during those highly driven phases, such as excessive spending or risky financial decisions?

Um... no, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't call it reckless. 

I guess sometimes when I'm really dialed in, I might, you know, buy some new software or maybe upgrade my home office setup. But that's just an investment in my productivity, right? It's not like I'm gambling or doing anything crazy with my savings. I'm a manager, so I'm used to handling budgets and making smart choices. 

Sure, maybe I spend a little more than usual when I'm feeling really energized, but it's always for a good reason. I'm very responsible with my finances. That makes sense, doesn't it? I just want to be clear that I'm not out of control or anything like that.
Do you usually experience a low or withdrawn period after one of your highly driven phases?

Um... well, yeah, I guess I do have some lower times. It's not like a crash or anything dramatic, I promise. It's just... 

Well, there are these stretches where I wake up and I just feel... heavy, I guess? Like I'm just a failed version of myself. I feel really flat, and honestly, even just answering my wife's normal, everyday questions feels like it takes so much effort. I just kind of retreat a little bit. 

But I still go to work! I mean, I still get things done, even if I'm not feeling my best. It's just a little harder to push through, that's all. Everyone gets a little burned out and needs to withdraw sometimes, right? I'm sure that's a pretty normal reaction to working hard. I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for... I'm really trying to be honest about it without making it sound worse than it is.
Do you ever feel like you're invincible or have an exaggerated sense of your own importance when you're in one of those highly driven phases?

Um... invincible? Oh, no, I wouldn't say invincible. That makes it sound like I think I'm a superhero or something, and I definitely don't. I just... well... 

I guess I do get very, very confident in my ideas. Maybe a little too intense about them sometimes? It's just that, when I'm really in that zone... I honestly believe I'm the only person who can see the whole IT architecture clearly. Like, the absolute only one who gets how it all connects. And I get this overwhelming feeling that if everyone would just listen to me and follow my plan, I could save the company from a major failure. 

I know how that sounds saying it out loud... a bit arrogant, maybe? I really don't want to come across like an egomaniac. I just care a lot about my job and want to protect our systems. That's... that's a good trait for a manager to have, right? Just being really dedicated to the big picture and taking ownership? I hope I'm explaining that okay, I just don't want you to think I'm completely full of myself.
Do you feel like you're more important or special when you're in one of those highly driven phases?

Um... well, I guess we kind of just touched on that, right? I don't know if I'd use the word "special," really. That makes it sound like I'm looking for a gold star or something. 

But, um... yeah, like I was saying, when I'm really at my peak during those times, I do get this intense feeling that I'm the absolute only one who can see the whole IT architecture clearly. It's like I have this bird's-eye view that everyone else is missing. And I really, honestly believe that if they would just get on board and follow my plan, I could save the company from a major, catastrophic failure. 

I know it sounds like a lot when I say it like that. I really don't want you to think I have a big ego or that I look down on my team. It's just... I get so passionate about making sure everything works perfectly. That's a pretty normal way for a dedicated manager to feel, isn't it? Just wanting to step up and fix things? I hope I'm making sense and not sounding too out of touch.
